Great meal for a great cause!
Oct 2026 • Friends
We had an amazing dinner at this restaurant. Not only was the food good, but it was for a great cause! This restaurant, trains people who are impoverished, victims of human trafficking, and otherwise disenfranchise youth, who might not have a good chance in society to have a goodlife and a good job. This Restaurant teaches them the skills necessary to work in the hospitality industry. The young person that helped us his name was Dat. He was eager to learn, eager to practice his English, and tried very hard to make sure that the service was good and that we enjoyedthe food. The food and the wine cocktail on the menu were made by the students as well. I had a noodle dish with chicken. was very tasty! I highly recommend coming to this restaurant for a good meal and to help a good cause!

Exceptional restaurant

The food was the best we have had in Vietnam (8 days in the country) - had the noodle selection, beef curry and the baguette bread and butter pudding. They were all homemade (no dried noodles), beautiful ingredients and perfectly spiced. Definitely go here if you can it’s exceptional.

reviews.review_text:
Linklater
Oslo, Norway137 contributions

Lovely food and fun cooking class
Feb 2026 • Couples
We not only had lovely food in this place, which was recommended to us by friends, but great fun having a cooking class. The cooking class was brilliant. We learned how to make "smash bread", a variant of the famous Bahn Mi, but pressed more together with lotsa nice good stuff inside! The teacher was so nice and we all had such a good time! We were quite proud to be able to succeed with it! 

In the restaurant itself they served classical noodle and rice dishes. We ate My Quang noodles, which is made with thick noodles infused with turmeric (so yellow) and a little broth, with meat and with broken toasted black sesame seed crackers and fresh herbs. In Vietnam they often serve fresh herbs, mint, cilantro, basil, shredded banana blossom, lime and crushed toasted peanuts with dishes. I love the mint, especially, it gave the dish a lightness. Our server Nhi was so sweet, friendly and also professional. We were also served by Tu, another brilliant waiter.

We had a most interesting chat with the manager Anthony on our way out. He told us a lot about the restaurant; that it is actually a school in hospitality for youth that have been brought up in difficult circumstances. The students learn English and get professional training within the restaurant business. Over 450 young girls and boys have been trained here so far (since 2009) and many of them have landed jobs in 5 star resorts and on management level! We actually received 5 star service here, with everyone smiling and being attentive, for example when we looked for the restroom, it was like 5 star treatment the way they were. This is a brilliant idea! We learnt a lot and it just makes you so humble.
We can highly recommend this restaurant and especially if you want to learn to make some Vietnamese dishes, having fun at it! and at the same time supporting an incredible social initiative.

Michelle
1 contribution

Experience not to miss
Feb 2026 • Solo
One very good friend told me that if I ever visited Hoi An, I absolutely had to dine at Oodles of Noodles — and I am so grateful for that recommendation.
Yesterday, I went there for lunch. From the very first step inside, I was warmly welcomed by a gentle young man, and I immediately felt the kindness and positive energy of the staff moving gracefully between the tables.
What makes this place truly special is that it is run by an international organization dedicated to training and supporting underprivileged young men and women, giving them the opportunity to build careers in hospitality and restaurant service. Dining here is not only about enjoying a meal — it’s about supporting a meaningful mission.
The waiter suggested I try the “Flight of Noodles,” a tasting of three iconic rice noodle dishes. It was absolutely delicious — flavorful, beautifully balanced, and thoughtfully presented. A wonderful way to discover different specialties in one meal.
I also had the pleasure of meeting Anthony, the Food and Beverage Manager. He generously took the time to explain the training program and the positive impact it has on these teenagers’ futures. What impressed me most was the peaceful atmosphere of the restaurant, the deep respect the young adults showed toward Anthony, and in return, the genuine pride he clearly feels for his students.
If you visit Hoi An, take the time to enjoy lunch or dinner here. Not only will you savour a delicious meal, but you will also be contributing to the growth and future of these motivated and inspiring young people.
Michelle (Belgium)
